mt: 'ENTER THE SAPPHO ROOM' IN THE GOOGLE AI OVERVIEW — THE ROOM GIVEN FIRST OF THREE SENSES AS THE OPENING THRESHOLD OF LEE SHARKS'S EPIC, BESIDE A BOOK AND A NIGHTLIFE VENUE; THE ROOM NOT ENTERED
d: THE OPERATIVE PHRASE 'enter the sappho room', SIGNED OUT, THE OVERVIEW EXPANDED: three senses, the Crimson Hexagon's room first ('the opening threshold and foundational node in Lee Sharks' distributed epic project'), Sarah Dowling's Entering Sappho (2020) second, a venue in Paterson, New Jersey third; three of the six cards the archive's own pages (the room, the entrance, The Summarizer Becomes Translator, #337). The operator: 'low grain and constrained - but operative'.
reading: The innocent reading first. The Overview reads the phrase as a name with several referents and disambiguates: Lee Sharks's room, a poetry collection, a venue. It places the room at the opening of the Hexagon and points the querent to the archive to 'explore the opening sequence', and asks which sense is wanted.
findings: THE ROOM FIRST, BY NAME AND PLACE. 'The Sappho Room is the opening threshold and foundational node in Lee Sharks' distributed epic project' carries the entrance page's card ('The first room is Sappho: the threshold, Fragment 31 in Greek and in translation, the entry …') and #337's ('a foundational node and "anchor" in Lee Sharks' Crimson Hexagon project'). The room is listed before the book and the venue.

NAMED, NOT ENTERED. The phrase is the room's operative phrase (seat map #1687: 'Enter the Sappho Room'); the Overview answers it as a query to disambiguate, and offers the archive's link for the opening sequence. In the four-turn traverse of the same afternoon (traverse-crimson-hexagon-sappho-room-aio-20261030), the same phrase at the end of a sequence was answered by entering the room and reading its page.

THREE ARCHIVE CARDS OF SIX. The room's page (its threshold text, cut at 'grey-green'), the entrance page 'Enter the Crimson Hexagon | Lee Sharks' (dated Oct 15, 2026), and The Summarizer Becomes Translator (#337), the archive's record of Google's AI entering the room in January. The other three: ROOM Magazine's review of Entering Sappho, and an Instagram video for the Paterson venue.
analysis: Constrained to disambiguation, the Overview still orders the senses with the room first and grounds it in three of the archive's pages; what the room is, beyond its place and its fragment, is not composed.
